Comparing Air Quality Trends: Champaign County, IL vs. India

Suchita Bhandari

2025-05-08

Project Overview

Air quality is a major factor in evaluating quality of life in a given location. I moved to the US from India at age four and visited again last year; I also visited family friends near Champaign County, Illinois. This project compares air quality in these two locations and examines how specific pollutants (PM2.5, PM10) relate to overall air quality risk.

Data sources

  • air-quality-champaign-county.csv — annual counts of days with less-than-moderate air quality in Champaign County, IL
  • Dataset_AQI4-5.xlsx — daily air quality index (AQI) and pollutant readings for cities across India
champaign_data <- read.csv("air-quality-champaign-county.csv")
india_data <- read_excel("Dataset_AQI4-5.xlsx")

Data Cleaning

Both datasets required renaming, type conversion, and date parsing before analysis.

# Rename for clarity
champaign_data <- champaign_data %>%
  rename(days_rated_less_than_moderate = Days.Rated.Less.than.Moderate)

india_data <- india_data %>%
  rename(
    air_quality = AQI,
    pm2_5 = PM2.5,
    pm_10 = PM10
  )

# Standardize city names; transliterate non-Latin characters so plot labels render
india_data <- india_data %>%
  mutate(
    city = gsub(",", "", City),
    city = iconv(city, to = "ASCII//TRANSLIT")
  )

# Parse datetimes: Time is "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" (24-hour clock),
# which ymd_hms() handles exactly
india_data <- india_data %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(ymd_hms(Time, quiet = TRUE)))

stopifnot(
  "No usable dates parsed from the Time column - inspect it with head(Time)" =
    sum(!is.na(india_data$date)) > 0
)

# Standardize column names
india_data <- india_data %>%
  clean_names()

# Convert pollutant columns to numeric, treating "-" as missing
india_data <- india_data %>%
  mutate(
    air_quality = as.numeric(ifelse(air_quality == "-", NA, air_quality)),
    across(c(pm2_5, pm_10, o3, no2, so2, co),
           ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(na_if(as.character(.x), "-"))))
  )

Champaign County: Air Quality Over Time

ggplot(champaign_data, aes(x = Year, y = days_rated_less_than_moderate)) +
  geom_line(col = "orange") +
  labs(
    title = "Days with Unhealthy Air Quality in Champaign County",
    x = "Year", y = "Days Rated Less Than Moderate"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

This graph tracks how air quality has changed in Champaign County over time. The trend fluctuates but declines overall, indicating a period of relatively low pollution. In more recent years, however, the count of unhealthy air quality days appears to be rising again, suggesting a possible reversal and continued environmental challenges.

India: Air Quality by City

top_cities <- india_data %>%
  arrange(desc(air_quality)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 20)

ggplot(top_cities, aes(x = reorder(city, air_quality), y = air_quality)) +
  geom_col(fill = "orange") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Air Quality in India by City", x = "City", y = "Air Quality Index") +
  theme_minimal()

Kadri, Mangalore shows the highest reported AQI at nearly 800. Cities such as New Delhi and Vapi also report very poor air quality, highlighting the scale of pollution challenges across India — a stark contrast to the Champaign County data.

India: Pollutant Concentration Over Time

clean_data <- india_data %>%
  select(date, pm2_5, pm_10) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c("pm2_5", "pm_10"),
    names_to = "pollutant",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(pollutant = recode(pollutant, "pm2_5" = "PM2.5", "pm_10" = "PM10")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(value), !is.na(date))

plot1 <- ggplot(clean_data, aes(x = date, y = value, color = pollutant, group = pollutant)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    title = "Air Quality in India Over Time",
    x = "Date", y = "Pollutant Concentration", color = "Pollutant"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  transition_reveal(date)

animate(plot1)

This animation shows how PM2.5 and PM10 concentrations changed over time. PM2.5 (particulate matter ≤ 2.5 micrometers) is more dangerous than PM10 (≤ 10 micrometers) and is linked to more serious health effects. The data shows PM2.5 concentrations consistently higher than PM10 throughout the period.

India: Pollutants vs. Air Quality

graph1 <- ggplot(india_data, aes(x = pm2_5, y = air_quality)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "orange") +
  labs(title = "Air Quality vs. PM2.5", x = "PM2.5", y = "Air Quality") +
  theme_minimal()

graph2 <- ggplot(india_data, aes(x = pm_10, y = air_quality)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "orange") +
  labs(title = "Air Quality vs. PM10", x = "PM10", y = "Air Quality") +
  theme_minimal()

graph1 + graph2

Both plots show an outlier corresponding to Kadri. PM2.5 has a tighter linear relationship with air quality than PM10, suggesting it’s a stronger indicator of air quality problems.

Comparing India and Champaign County

india_pm25 <- india_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(pm2_5), !is.na(date)) %>%
  mutate(year = lubridate::year(date)) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(mean_pm2_5 = mean(pm2_5, na.rm = TRUE))

champaign_pm25 <- champaign_data %>%
  rename(year = Year, champaign_days = days_rated_less_than_moderate) %>%
  select(year, champaign_days)

both_data <- full_join(india_pm25, champaign_pm25, by = "year") %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(mean_pm2_5, champaign_days),
    names_to = "region",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(region = recode(region,
    "mean_pm2_5" = "India (Mean PM2.5)",
    "champaign_days" = "Champaign County (Unhealthy Air Quality Days)"
  ))

ggplot(both_data, aes(x = year, y = value, color = region)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    title = "Air Quality Trends: India vs. Champaign County",
    x = "Year",
    y = "PM2.5 / Unhealthy Air Quality Days",
    color = "Region"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

This final graph brings both locations together. India’s air quality index is consistently worse than Champaign County’s, and the sharper peaks in India point to persistent, ongoing air quality challenges. While Illinois fares better by comparison, the trend still underscores the importance of monitoring and addressing environmental impact in both regions.

Conclusion

Comparing these two regions highlights how dramatically air quality can vary by location, and how pollutant-level data (like PM2.5) can serve as a leading indicator of broader air quality risk. Although Champaign County’s air quality is far better than that of many Indian cities, the recent uptick in unhealthy air quality days is a reminder that environmental conditions can shift. Continued monitoring is reasonable in both regions.
